# Benchmarks & Evaluation

> Benchmarks, evaluation suites and leaderboards for embodied agents, reasoning models and VLAs.  
> Layer: L6 · 115 entries · [overview](../README.md#benchmark) · [survey](../SURVEY.md)

**Legend:** 🟢 open · 🟡 partial · 🔵 api · ⚪ closed. Hover a name for the full paper title. Newest first within each year.

**2026**

- ⚪ [**VLA behavioural robustness**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01351 "Is Success All You Need? Investigating the Impact of Input Perturbations on VLA Behaviour in Tabletop Manipulation Tasks") · 2026-10 — Benchmark-agnostic evaluation extending LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus that measures how perturbations change successful trajectories (smoothness, efficiency, gripper behaviour), showing that equal success rates can hide divergent behaviour.
- 🟢 [**HumanoidToolBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02089 "HumanoidToolBench: Benchmarking Humanoid Tool Use from Selection to Mobile Execution") · 2026-10 — 18-task benchmark of humanoid tool use from tool selection to mobile execution, with the ToolBook dataset of 3.1k demonstrations from simulation and a real Unitree G1; finds large gaps between picking a suitable tool and completing the task. [code](https://github.com/SNU-PI/HumanoidToolBench) · [project](https://snu-pi.github.io/HumanoidToolBench/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/snupilab/humanoidtoolbench-teleop)
- 🟢 [**Embodied Agent Arena**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00854 "Are Frontier VLM Agents Ready to Be Robot Generalists? An Empirical Study with the Embodied Agent Arena") · 2026-10 — 1,000-case arena drawn from 32 sources plus a new GeoProbe geometry benchmark, run through a minimal harness that separates metric precision, functional grounding and native goal completion across geometry, spatial reasoning, affordance, planning and manipulation; seven VLMs evaluated. [code](https://github.com/embodied-agent-arena/embodied-agent-arena) · [project](https://embodied-agent-arena.github.io/embodied-agent-arena/)
- ⚪ [**Ego2Act**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01092 "Ego2Act: Evaluating Goal-Directed Manipulation in Egocentric Video Generation") · 2026-10 — Benchmark of 2,640 videos from 110 real-world tasks testing whether video generation models, used as world simulators, can produce egocentric videos of multi-step goal-directed hand manipulation; adds an automatic judge, Ego2ActJudge.
- ⚪ [**X2Real**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27449 "X2Real: an eXtensive simulation benchmark for real-world generalist policies") · 2026-09 · X Square Robot — Evolvable simulation benchmark on Isaac Lab-Arena calibrated to real hardware, with 10 capability dimensions and 44 hierarchical long-horizon tasks, multi-axis domain randomization, strictly disjoint train/eval pipelines and ~300 hours of annotated sim trajectories. _Note: First-party 0.84 linear correlation between simulated and real-robot results. The paper's code link (github.com/X-Square-Robot/x2real) returned 404 on 2026-09-29._
- ⚪ [**WorldAuditBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40325 "WorldAuditBench: Interactive 3D World Auditing with Multimodal Agents") · 2026-09 — 213 anomaly-auditing tasks in 13 Unreal Engine 5 and Three.js worlds (floating objects, traversable walls and more) that test whether multimodal agents can couple exploration with visual reasoning; frontier models score well below humans.
- ⚪ [**VLA acceleration benchmark audit**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37771 "Faster and Better? Benchmark Bugs and Design Limitations Distort the Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Acceleration") · 2026-09 — Audits seven simulated manipulation benchmarks, including RoboTwin, LIBERO-Plus and VLABench, finding 22 bugs and 4 design limitations that let VLA acceleration methods beat their own baselines; fixes can reverse method rankings. _Note: The paper says the fixes are released; no repository link was found (checked 2026-10-01)._
- 🟡 [**Video2Skill**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36691 "Video2Skill: From Streaming Experience to Reusable Embodied Skills") · 2026-09 — Benchmark for streaming embodied skill discovery: a VLM watches robot and human manipulation videos in sequence and must locate events, group same-transformation events and decide when to reuse or create a skill in a persistent library. [project](https://andyzworks.github.io/video2skill/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Sterzhang/video2skill-bench)

[code](https://github.com/SciHorizon-elab/SciHorizon-elab)
- ⚪ [**RoboIRGBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34384 "RoboIRGBench: Benchmarking Implicit Referential Grounding in Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2026-09 — Manipulation benchmark built on RoboMME (40 variants of 11 tasks) testing whether VLAs recover implicitly referenced objects, quantities and relations from context; finds sharp drops versus explicit instructions. [project](https://aernar.github.io/RoboIRGBench/)
- 🟢 [**RoboFollow**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25636 "RoboFollow: Unveiling the Instruction Following Mirage in Embodied Agents") · 2026-09 — Diagnostic benchmark showing high success rates overstate instruction following: training scenes admit several kinematically distinct tasks, and a four-level protocol perturbs layout and semantics; across nine VLA and WAM policies, strong base-level scores did not reliably transfer to the harder levels. [code](https://github.com/AutoLab-SAI-SJTU/RoboFollow) · [project](https://mrc-crm.github.io/RoboFollow/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AutoLab-SJTU/robofollow-data)
- 🟢 [**RLE-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34210 "RLE-Bench: A Qualifying Exam for Coding Agents as Robot Learning Engineers") · 2026-09 — Benchmark that evaluates coding agents as robot-learning engineers across interactive control, policy learning, perception and estimation, and mechanical design, scoring the artifacts they submit (policies, harnesses, designs) into an overall RLE Index. [code](https://github.com/RLE-Bench/RLE-Bench) · [project](https://rle-bench.github.io/)

Report finds offline action-prediction metrics poorly forecast closed-loop success._ [project](https://www.kdc.icra.lejurobot.com/)
- ⚪ [**OmniEcho**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23407 "OmniEcho: Audio-Visual Spatial Understanding for Omni-Modal Embodied Agents") · 2026-09 — OmniEchoBench: six spatial audio-visual tasks over 197 real scenes plus 900 sound-guided navigation samples with first-order ambisonics audio; also an omni-modal model with an FOA spatial encoder. _Note: Repository lists data and evaluation code as coming soon (checked 2026-10-04)._ [code](https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/OmniEcho)
- ⚪ [**MotionForge**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25689 "MotionForge: A Data Generation Pipeline and Large-Scale Benchmark for Long-Horizon Manipulation of Dynamic Objects with Domain Shifts") · 2026-09 · Nanyang Technological University et al. — Simulation benchmark and data pipeline for dynamic-object manipulation: 40 tasks over 11 motion patterns (17 long-horizon), single- and joint-domain-shift protocols, and latency-aware execution in which the scene keeps moving during policy inference. _Note: No code link found (v1 2026-09-22)._
- 🟢 [**MEMOBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07047 "MEMOBench: A Process Level Memory Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation") · 2026-09 · Zhejiang University — Process-level memory benchmark on LIBERO: 30 history-dependent tasks, 1,500 demos and 4,200 executable checkpoints labelling memory storage, update and compression, so forgetting is scored separately from manipulation failure. _Note: See also RMBench (arXiv 2603.01229, https://rmbench.github.io/), a 9-task memory-dependent manipulation benchmark._ [code](https://github.com/Collab-Gen/MEMOBench) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SunSeaLucky/MEMOBench)
- 🟢 [**LIBERO-Recover**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05178 "LIBERO-RECOVER: Beyond Task Success Towards Failure Recovery in Robotic Manipulation Models") · 2026-09 — Failure-recovery benchmark built on LIBERO from real execution failures of state-of-the-art models, with 1,000+ scenarios across four levels: action retry, action adaptation, object-state recovery and environmental recovery. _Note: Could equally sit under verification (recovery as an exit-code capability)._ [code](https://github.com/liulin815/LIBERO-Recovery) · [project](https://liulin815.github.io/LIBERO-Recovery/)
- 🟢 [**LIBERO-MAX**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36518 "LIBERO-MAX: Do Robot Policies Adapt When the World Changes?") · 2026-09 — 8,000 paired cases that inject a mid-task change (moved target, viewpoint shift, clutter, obstacle, and more) and compare against the same rollout without it, isolating event-caused regressions across 14 VLA, hybrid and world-action policies. - ⚪ [**JRDB-AVR**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35032 "JRDB-AVR: An Active Visual Reasoning Benchmark for Embodied Agents in Real-World Environments") · 2026-09 — Active visual reasoning benchmark built from real JRDB robot data: agents request bounded observations by timestamp and viewpoint and are scored on both the answer and the grounded evidence; includes a reference agent with a graph-based world model. _Note: NeurIPS 2026. - ⚪ [**HappyWorld-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24308) · 2026-09 — World-model benchmark that tests whether generated worlds stay consistent and responsive under exploration, interaction and modification, with video, spatial and embodied tracks, automated metrics and an Elo arena of human A/B comparisons.
- ⚪ [**HALTER**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19413 "From Rollout to Reset: A Graph-Based Harness for Autonomous Long-Horizon Manipulation Evaluation") · 2026-09 — Harness for autonomous long-horizon evaluation and reset: it builds a spatial scene graph online and restores the scene by planning over a library of learned atomic reset skills, extending AutoEval-style unattended evaluation beyond single-step tasks. _Note: First-party: restores the scene in 76% of episodes vs 52% for AutoEval on four Franka tasks._

- ⚪ [**LIBERO-X**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06556 "LIBERO-X: Robustness Litmus for Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2026-02 · Beihang University; Meituan — LIBERO-based VLA benchmark with a hierarchical, progressively harder protocol for spatial generalization, object recognition and instruction understanding, plus a diverse teleoperated training set to narrow the train-evaluation distribution gap. _Note: RSS 2026. The GitHub repo currently hosts only the project page; no benchmark code yet._ [project](https://zackhxn.github.io/LIBERO-X/)
- 🟢 [**Isaac Lab-Arena**](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/simplify-generalist-robot-policy-evaluation-in-simulation-with-nvidia-isaac-lab-arena/) · 2026-01 · NVIDIA — Open-source Isaac Lab extension for benchmark authoring and large-scale policy evaluation that composes environments from scene, embodiment and task modules; NVIDIA cites RoboCasa and LIBERO task integrations and GPU-parallel evaluation. _Note: Alpha (v0.3) per README; date is the NVIDIA launch blog (Jan 2026)._ [code](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena) · [docs](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab-Arena/main/index.html)

**2025**

- 🟢 [**VLNVerse**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19021 "VLNVerse: A Benchmark for Vision-Language Navigation with Versatile, Embodied, Realistic Simulation and Evaluation") · 2025-12 · Adelaide University; Shanghai AI Lab et al. — Large-scale vision-language navigation benchmark that unifies fragmented VLN tasks with fully embodied agents in physics-based realistic simulation, evaluating classic and MLLM-based navigators plus a unified multi-task model. _Note: The code repository is the one the official project page instructs users to clone._ [code](https://github.com/william13077/IAmGoodNavigator) · [project](https://sihaoevery.github.io/vlnverse/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Eyz/VLNVerse_data)
- 🟢 [**PolaRiS**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.16881 "PolaRiS: Scalable Real-to-Sim Evaluations for Generalist Robot Policies") · 2025-12 — Real-to-sim evaluation framework that turns short video scans of real scenes into interactive simulation via neural reconstruction, plus a sim co-training recipe; paired tests show closer agreement with real-world rankings than prior sim benchmarks. _Note: Correlation results are first-party._ [code](https://github.com/arhanjain/PolaRiS) · [project](https://polaris-evals.github.io)
- 🟢 [**World-in-World**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18135 "World-in-World: World Models in a Closed-Loop World") · 2025-10 — Open platform that benchmarks generative world models by closed-loop embodied task success rather than visual quality, with a unified online-planning strategy and action API over four environments; finds controllability matters more than visual fidelity. [code](https://github.com/World-In-World/world-in-world) · [project](https://world-in-world.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**RobotArena ∞**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23571 "RobotArena ∞: Scalable Robot Benchmarking via Real-to-Sim Translation") · 2025-10 · Carnegie Mellon University; National Taiwan University — Converts video demonstrations from widely used robot datasets into simulated digital twins (VLMs, 2D-to-3D generation, differentiable rendering) and scores VLA policies with VLM-guided metrics plus crowdsourced pairwise human preferences under controlled perturbations. [code](https://github.com/offjangir/RobotArena) · [project](https://robotarenainf.github.io)
- 🟡 [**RoboChallenge**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17950 "RoboChallenge: Large-scale Real-robot Evaluation of Embodied Policies") · 2025-10 · Dexmal; Hugging Face — Online real-robot evaluation service for VLA policies; its first benchmark, Table30, has 30 tabletop manipulation tasks across several robot embodiments, with results aggregated on a public leaderboard. _Note: Table30 V2 was presented at the CVPR 2026 GigaBrain Challenge workshop._ [project](https://robochallenge.ai) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/RoboChallenge/Table30)
- 🟢 [**RoboBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17801 "Robobench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain") · 2025-10 · Peking University et al. — Evaluates MLLMs as the System-2 embodied brain with 6,092 QA pairs over 14 capabilities in five dimensions: instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction and failure analysis, drawn from real robot data. _Note: ECCV 2026._ [code](https://github.com/yulin-luo/RoboBench) · [project](https://robo-bench.github.io) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/LeoFan01/RoboBench)
- 🟢 [**LIBERO-PRO**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03827 "LIBERO-PRO: Towards Robust and Fair Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Models Beyond Memorization") · 2025-10 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology et al. — Extends LIBERO with perturbations to manipulated objects, initial states, instructions and environments; first-party results show VLAs scoring over 90% on standard LIBERO collapse in the generalized setting, exposing memorized trajectories. [code](https://github.com/Zxy-MLlab/LIBERO-PRO) · [project](https://zxy-mllab.github.io/LIBERO-PRO-Webpage/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/zhouxueyang/LIBERO-Pro)
- 🟢 [**LIBERO-Plus**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13626 "LIBERO-Plus: In-depth Robustness Analysis of Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2025-10 · Fudan University et al. — Robustness suite that perturbs LIBERO along seven axes (object layout, camera viewpoint, robot initial state, language, lighting, background, sensor noise); finds VLAs highly sensitive to viewpoint and initial state and often ignoring language. _Note: CVPR 2026 version titled "LIBERO-Plus: A Progressive Robustness Benchmark for Visual-Language-Action Models"._ [code](https://github.com/sylvestf/LIBERO-plus) · [project](https://sylvestf.github.io/LIBERO-plus/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Sylvest/LIBERO-plus)
- 🟢 [**BEAR**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08759 "Dissecting Embodied Abilities in Multimodal Language Models through Skill-level Evaluation and Diagnosis") · 2025-10 · Peking University; Northeastern University et al. — Skill-level benchmark that decomposes embodied tasks into 14 atomic skills in 6 categories (4,469 image-video-text samples) from low-level perception to high-level planning; evaluating 20 MLLMs shows perception is a major bottleneck behind reasoning failures. _Note: ICML 2026. arXiv v1 was titled "BEAR: Benchmarking and Enhancing Multimodal Language Models for Atomic Embodied Capabilities"; also proposes BEAR-Agent, a tool-augmented MLLM agent._ [code](https://github.com/yqi19/BEAR-official) · [project](https://bear-official66.github.io/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yqi19/BEAR-benchmark)
- 🟢 [**VLA-Arena**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22539 "VLA-Arena: An Open-Source Framework for Benchmarking Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2025-09 · Peking University; BAAI — VLA benchmark of 170 tasks in 11 suites over safety, distractor, extrapolation and long-horizon dimensions, with three difficulty levels (fine-tuning only on L0) and orthogonal language/visual perturbations; ships datasets and a public leaderboard. _Note: Code released 2025-09 (per repo); paper 2025-12; ICML 2026._ [code](https://github.com/PKU-Alignment/VLA-Arena) · [project](https://vla-arena.github.io)
- ⚪ [**Embodied Arena**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.15273 "Embodied Arena: A Comprehensive, Unified, and Evolving Evaluation Platform for Embodied AI") · 2025-09 · Tianjin University; Huawei Noah's Ark Lab et al. — Unified evaluation platform with a capability taxonomy (perception, reasoning, task execution) that integrates 22 benchmarks and 30+ models, an LLM-driven pipeline for evolving test data, and live leaderboards for embodied QA, navigation and task planning. _Note: Leaderboards are public on the site; no platform code release found._ [project](https://www.embodied-arena.com/)
- ⚪ [**Benjie's Humanoid Olympic Games**](https://generalrobots.substack.com/p/benjies-humanoid-olympic-games) · 2025-09 · Benjie Holson (General Robots newsletter) — Informal challenge list of household manipulation events (full-body, laundry, tool use, fingertips, wet tasks) with bronze/silver/gold tiers, proposed as a yardstick for general-purpose robot manipulation.
- ⚪ [**Kitchen-R**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15663 "Mind and Motion Aligned: A Joint Evaluation IsaacSim Benchmark for Task Planning and Low-Level Policies in Mobile Manipulation") · 2025-08 · Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology et al. — Isaac Sim digital-twin kitchen benchmark with 500+ language instructions for a mobile manipulator that scores the VLM task planner, the low-level policy, and the integrated planner-plus-policy system in three separate modes. _Note: No code link found._
- 🟢 [**RoboEval**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00435 "RoboEval: Where Robotic Manipulation Meets Structured and Scalable Evaluation") · 2025-07 · Allen Institute for AI et al. — Structured manipulation evaluation that augments binary success with behavioral and outcome metrics (efficiency, coordination, safety/stability, stage progress, failure localization) over eight bimanual tasks with controlled variations and 3,000+ demos. [code](https://github.com/Robo-Eval/RoboEval) · [project](https://robo-eval.github.io)
- 🟢 [**RoboCerebra**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06677 "RoboCerebra: A Large-scale Benchmark for Long-horizon Robotic Manipulation Evaluation") · 2025-06 · Beihang University; National University of Singapore; Shanghai Jiao Tong University — Long-horizon manipulation benchmark for System-2 reasoning: a large simulated household dataset with long subtask sequences, a VLM-planner plus VLA-controller hierarchy, and a protocol that scores planning, reflection and memory. _Note: NeurIPS 2025._ [code](https://github.com/qiuboxiang/RoboCerebra) · [project](https://robocerebra.github.io/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/qiukingballball/RoboCerebraBench)
- 🟢 [**RoboArena**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.18123 "RoboArena: Distributed Real-World Evaluation of Generalist Robot Policies") · 2025-06 — Crowd-sourced real-world evaluation: evaluators at several institutions run double-blind pairwise comparisons of generalist policies on DROID robots in self-chosen tasks, and preferences are aggregated into a policy ranking open to community submissions. _Note: First-party study used 600+ pairwise episodes across seven policies at seven institutions._ [code](https://github.com/robo-arena/roboarena) · [project](https://robo-arena.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**RefSpatial-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04308 "RoboRefer: Towards Spatial Referring with Reasoning in Vision-Language Models for Robotics") · 2025-06 · BAAI et al. — Spatial-referring benchmark introduced with RoboRefer: VLMs must point to objects or free-space targets described by multi-step spatial relations in cluttered real scenes, with location, placement and unseen-relation splits. _Note: The RoboRefer README reports use in Qwen3-VL and Gemini Robotics 1.5 evaluations and a later RefSpatial-Expand-Bench with outdoor scenes. RoboRefer (model) belongs under brain._ [code](https://github.com/Zhoues/RoboRefer) · [project](https://zhoues.github.io/RoboRefer/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/BAAI/RefSpatial-Bench)
- 🟢 [**OmniSpatial**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03135 "OmniSpatial: Towards Comprehensive Spatial Reasoning Benchmark for Vision Language Models") · 2025-06 · Tsinghua University; Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute et al. — Spatial-reasoning benchmark grounded in cognitive psychology with 8.4K+ QA pairs over dynamic reasoning, complex spatial logic, spatial interaction and perspective-taking (50 subcategories); also tests scene-graph and novel-view chain-of-thought aids. _Note: ICLR 2026._ [code](https://github.com/qizekun/OmniSpatial) · [project](https://qizekun.github.io/omnispatial/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/qizekun/OmniSpatial)
- 🟢 [**INT-ACT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09930 "From Intention to Execution: Probing the Generalization Boundaries of Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2025-06 · New York University — Probing suite of 50 simulated tasks in 10 subcategories over language, vision and object shifts; finds VLAs keep coherent intentions out of distribution but fail at precise execution, and that action fine-tuning can erode the backbone VLM's reasoning. [code](https://github.com/ai4ce/INT-ACT) · [project](https://ai4ce.github.io/INT-ACT/)
- 🟢 [**PointArena**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09990 "PointArena: Probing Multimodal Grounding Through Language-Guided Pointing") · 2025-05 · Allen Institute for AI et al. — Language-guided pointing evaluation in three parts: Point-Bench (~1,000 curated tasks in five reasoning categories), Point-Battle (blind pairwise web arena with human votes) and Point-Act (a real robot executing actions from model-predicted points). [code](https://github.com/pointarena/pointarena) · [project](https://pointarena.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**MMSI-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23764 "MMSI-Bench: A Benchmark for Multi-Image Spatial Intelligence") · 2025-05 · Shanghai AI Laboratory; CUHK et al. — Multi-image spatial-intelligence VQA benchmark of 1,000 expert-written multiple-choice questions from 120,000+ images with annotated reasoning; first-party results put humans at 97% versus about 40% for the best model tested. _Note: ICLR 2026._ [code](https://github.com/OpenRobotLab/MMSI-Bench) · [project](https://runsenxu.com/projects/MMSI_Bench)
- 🟡 [**AgiBot World Challenge**](https://opendrivelab.com/challenge2025/) · 2025-05 · AgiBot; OpenDriveLab — Annual competition on AgiBot World data: the IROS 2025 edition had a manipulation track (online sim round, then real-robot final) and a world-model track; the ICRA 2026 edition runs Reasoning-to-Action and World Model tracks. _Note: 2025 edition launched late May 2025 with the on-site final at IROS 2025 (Hangzhou)._ [blog](https://www.agibot.com/article/231/detail/45.html) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/agibot-world/AgiBotWorldChallenge-2025)
- ⚪ [**STAR-Gen**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01238 "A Taxonomy for Evaluating Generalist Robot Manipulation Policies") · 2025-03 · Stanford University; Google DeepMind — Taxonomy of generalization for manipulation policies along visual, semantic and behavioral axes with reproducible measurement guidelines, instantiated as real-world benchmarks on Bridge V2 (BridgeV2-★) and the bimanual ALOHA 2 platform. _Note: RA-L. Per the project page, BridgeV2-★ has 4 base tasks and 55 variations over 13 axes (885 real-world evaluations of OpenVLA, MiniVLA and pi0)._ [project](https://stargen-taxonomy.github.io)
- 🟢 [**RoboFactory**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16408 "RoboFactory: Exploring Embodied Agent Collaboration with Compositional Constraints") · 2025-03 — Proposes compositional constraints and interfaces for embodied multi-agent systems, an automated data collection framework built on them, and the first embodied multi-agent manipulation benchmark, with multi-agent imitation-learning baselines. [code](https://github.com/MARS-EAI/RoboFactory) · [project](https://iranqin.github.io/robofactory/)
- 🟢 [**EXPRESS-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.11117 "Beyond the Destination: A Novel Benchmark for Exploration-Aware Embodied Question Answering") · 2025-03 · Sun Yat-sen University et al. — Exploration-aware embodied QA benchmark with 777 exploration trajectories and 2,044 question-trajectory pairs, plus an Exploration-Answer Consistency metric that checks answers are grounded in what the agent actually explored. _Note: ICCV 2025; also introduces the Fine-EQA exploration baseline._ [code](https://github.com/HCPLab-SYSU/EXPRESS-Bench)
- 🟢 [**ERQA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20020 "Gemini Robotics: Bringing AI into the Physical World") · 2025-03 · Google DeepMind — Embodied Reasoning QA: multiple-choice questions with interleaved images and text on spatial reasoning and world knowledge in robotics scenarios, released with Gemini Robotics together with a lightweight evaluation harness for multimodal model APIs. _Note: Introduced in the Gemini Robotics tech report; the models themselves belong under brain/policy._ [code](https://github.com/embodiedreasoning/ERQA) · [blog](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/gemini-robotics-brings-ai-into-the-physical-world/)
- 🟢 [**AutoEval**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.24278 "AutoEval: Autonomous Evaluation of Generalist Robot Manipulation Policies in the Real World") · 2025-03 · UC Berkeley — Job-queue system that evaluates submitted robot policies around the clock, supplying automatic success detection and automatic scene resets; public Bridge/WidowX AutoEval cells are open to the community. _Note: CoRL 2025. Success detection here acts as the evaluation 'exit code'; could also sit under benchmark._ [code](https://github.com/zhouzypaul/auto_eval) · [project](https://auto-eval.github.io/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/zhouzypaul/auto_eval)
- 🟢 [**EmbodiedBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09560 "EmbodiedBench: Comprehensive Benchmarking Multi-modal Large Language Models for Vision-Driven Embodied Agents") · 2025-02 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign et al. — Evaluates MLLMs as vision-driven embodied agents on 1,128 tasks in four environments (EB-ALFRED, EB-Habitat, EB-Navigation, EB-Manipulation), from high-level household planning to low-level atomic actions, with capability-specific subsets. _Note: ICML 2025 (oral); project page hosts a leaderboard._ [code](https://github.com/EmbodiedBench/EmbodiedBench) · [project](https://embodiedbench.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**PhysBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16411 "PhysBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Vision-Language Models for Physical World Understanding") · 2025-01 · University of Southern California et al. — 10,002 interleaved video-image-text items testing VLM understanding of the physical world across object properties, object relationships, scene understanding and physics-based dynamics; 75 VLMs evaluated. _Note: ICLR 2025._ [code](https://github.com/USC-GVL/PhysBench) · [project](https://physbench.github.io/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/USC-GVL/PhysBench)
- 🟢 [**EmbodiedEval**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.11858 "EmbodiedEval: Evaluate Multimodal LLMs as Embodied Agents") · 2025-01 · Tsinghua University — Interactive benchmark for MLLMs as embodied agents: 328 tasks in 125 3D scenes spanning navigation, object interaction, social interaction and attribute/spatial QA, all run in one unified simulation and evaluation framework. A Holistic Embodied Cognition Benchmark") · 2025-01 · Zhejiang University; Alibaba DAMO Academy et al. — Egocentric-video benchmark of embodied cognition for LVLMs across 30 dimensions, including robot self-cognition, dynamic scene perception and hallucination, with human-annotated open-ended questions and the ECEval evaluation system. [code](https://github.com/Rh-Dang/ECBench)

- 🟢 [**VSI-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14171 "Thinking in Space: How Multimodal Large Language Models See, Remember, and Recall Spaces") · 2024-12 · New York University; Yale University; Stanford University — Video-based visual-spatial intelligence benchmark with 5,000+ QA pairs over indoor scene videos, probing whether MLLMs build and recall spatial layouts; finds explicit cognitive maps help while chain-of-thought style prompting does not. [code](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/VLABench) · [project](https://vlabench.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**ManiSkill-HAB (MS-HAB)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.13211 "ManiSkill-HAB: A Benchmark for Low-Level Manipulation in Home Rearrangement Tasks") · 2024-12 · UC San Diego; Hillbot — GPU-accelerated reimplementation of the Home Assistant Benchmark for low-level manipulation and in-home rearrangement with realistic control, RL/IL baselines, and rule-based filtering of RL trajectories for controlled large-scale demonstration generation. [code](https://github.com/arth-shukla/mshab) · [project](https://arth-shukla.github.io/mshab)

- 🟢 [**LAMBDA (λ)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05313 "λ: A Benchmark for Data-Efficiency in Long-Horizon Indoor Mobile Manipulation Robotics") · 2024-11 — Data-efficiency benchmark for language-conditioned, long-horizon, multi-room and multi-floor mobile pick-and-place with 571 human-collected demonstrations in simulation and the real world; a neuro-symbolic TAMP approach outperforms end-to-end learners. _Note: IROS 2025._ [code](https://github.com/h2r/NPM-Dataset) · [project](https://lambdabenchmark.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**PARTNR**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00081 "PARTNR: A Benchmark for Planning and Reasoning in Embodied Multi-agent Tasks") · 2024-10 · Meta FAIR — Human-robot collaboration benchmark of 100,000 natural-language household tasks in Habitat (60 houses, 5,819 objects), generated with LLMs and simulation-in-the-loop checks; finds LLM planners coordinate and recover from errors poorly. [code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/partnr-planner) · [project](https://aihabitat.org/partnr/)
- 🟢 [**GemBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01345 "Towards Generalizable Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation: A Benchmark and LLM-guided 3D Policy") · 2024-10 · Inria; ENS-PSL — Generalization benchmark for vision-language manipulation with seven action primitives and four levels (novel placements, rigid objects, articulated objects, long-horizon tasks); introduced with 3D-LOTUS and the LLM/VLM-guided 3D-LOTUS++. _Note: ICRA 2025._ [code](https://github.com/vlc-robot/robot-3dlotus) · [project](https://www.di.ens.fr/willow/research/gembench/)
- ⚪ [**ET-Plan-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14682 "ET-Plan-Bench: Embodied Task-level Planning Benchmark Towards Spatial-Temporal Cognition with Foundation Models") · 2024-10 · Huawei Noah's Ark Lab — Embodied task-planning benchmark for LLMs with controllable difficulty that probes spatial constraints (relations, occlusion) and temporal/causal understanding; simulator backends return feedback so the model can re-plan during interaction. _Note: No public code release found._
- 🟢 [**Embodied Agent Interface (EAI)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07166 "Embodied Agent Interface: Benchmarking LLMs for Embodied Decision Making") · 2024-10 · Stanford University; Northwestern University; Amazon; MIT — Standardized interface and benchmark that splits LLM embodied decision making into goal interpretation, subgoal decomposition, action sequencing and transition modeling, with fine-grained error metrics (hallucination, affordance, planning) on BEHAVIOR and VirtualHome. _Note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track (oral)._ [code](https://github.com/embodied-agent-interface/embodied-agent-interface) · [project](https://embodied-agent-interface.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**Where2Place**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10721 "RoboPoint: A Vision-Language Model for Spatial Affordance Prediction for Robotics") · 2024-06 · University of Washington; NVIDIA — Pointing benchmark for spatial free-space reference on challenging real-world images (e.g., where to place an object relative to others), released with RoboPoint to score robot-oriented VLMs that answer with image points. _Note: Introduced in the RoboPoint paper; the RoboPoint model itself belongs under brain._ [code](https://github.com/wentaoyuan/RoboPoint) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/wentao-yuan/where2place)
- 🟢 [**EmbSpatial-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05756 "EmbSpatial-Bench: Benchmarking Spatial Understanding for Embodied Tasks with Large Vision-Language Models") · 2024-06 · Fudan University — Embodied spatial-understanding benchmark for LVLMs derived automatically from embodied 3D scenes, covering six egocentric spatial relationships; released with the EmbSpatial-SFT instruction-tuning set. _Note: ACL 2024._ [code](https://github.com/mengfeidu/EmbSpatial-Bench)
- 🟢 [**SimplerEnv (SIMPLER)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05941 "Evaluating Real-World Robot Manipulation Policies in Simulation") · 2024-05 — Simulated environments matched to common real setups (Google Robot, WidowX/Bridge) that reduce control and visual sim-to-real gaps; paired evaluations show strong correlation with real-world policy performance and failure modes. [code](https://github.com/simpler-env/SimplerEnv) · [project](https://simpler-env.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**OpenEQA**](https://open-eqa.github.io/ "OpenEQA: Embodied Question Answering in the Era of Foundation Models") · 2024-04 · Meta FAIR — Open-vocabulary embodied question answering benchmark with 1,600+ human-written questions from 180+ real-world environments, covering episodic-memory and active-exploration settings, scored with an LLM-based automatic metric. _Note: CVPR 2024; not on arXiv (paper PDF hosted on the project page)._ [code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/open-eqa) · [blog](https://ai.meta.com/blog/openeqa-embodied-question-answering-robotics-ar-glasses/)
- 🟢 [**GOAT-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06609 "GOAT-Bench: A Benchmark for Multi-Modal Lifelong Navigation") · 2024-04 · Georgia Tech et al. — Multi-modal lifelong navigation benchmark ("GO to AnyThing"): agents reach sequences of goals given as category names, language descriptions or images, used to study explicit versus implicit scene memory. [code](https://github.com/Ram81/goat-bench) · [project](https://mukulkhanna.github.io/goat-bench/)
- 🟢 [**HumanoidBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10506 "HumanoidBench: Simulated Humanoid Benchmark for Whole-Body Locomotion and Manipulation") · 2024-03 · UC Berkeley; Yonsei University — Simulated benchmark for a humanoid with dexterous hands covering whole-body locomotion and manipulation; state-of-the-art RL struggles on most tasks while hierarchical policies built on robust low-level skills do better. [code](https://github.com/carlosferrazza/humanoid-bench) · [project](https://humanoid-bench.github.io)
- 🟢 [**BEHAVIOR-1K / OmniGibson**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09227 "BEHAVIOR-1K: A Human-Centered, Embodied AI Benchmark with 1,000 Everyday Activities and Realistic Simulation") · 2024-03 · Stanford University — 1,000 everyday household activities in 50 scenes with 9,000+ annotated objects, simulated in OmniGibson (rigid and deformable bodies, liquids); the BEHAVIOR Challenge (NeurIPS 2025: 50 long-horizon mobile-manipulation tasks; 2026: 100 tasks) runs a public leaderboard. _Note: Preliminary version at CoRL 2022; the OmniGibson repo now resolves to the BEHAVIOR-1K monorepo._ [code](https://github.com/StanfordVL/BEHAVIOR-1K) · [project](https://behavior.stanford.edu/)
- 🟢 [**THE COLOSSEUM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08191 "THE COLOSSEUM: A Benchmark for Evaluating Generalization for Robotic Manipulation") · 2024-02 — Extends 20 RLBench tasks with 14 axes of environmental perturbation (color, texture, size, lighting, distractors, physics, camera pose); first-party results show 30-50% success drops per factor and 75%+ when combined, correlated with real-world perturbations. _Note: RSS 2024. Successor Colosseum V2 (arXiv 2605.27759, RA-L; https://colosseum-v2.github.io/) moves to ManiSkill with 28 tasks and two robot morphologies for VLA generalization._ [code](https://github.com/robot-colosseum/robot-colosseum) · [project](https://robot-colosseum.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**LoTa-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08178 "LoTa-Bench: Benchmarking Language-oriented Task Planners for Embodied Agents") · 2024-02 · ETRI — Benchmark system that automatically scores LLM task planners for home-service robots by executing their plans in ALFRED/AI2-THOR and an extended Watch-And-Help/VirtualHome, used to study model choice and prompt construction. _Note: ICLR 2024._ [code](https://github.com/lbaa2022/LLMTaskPlanning)
- 🟢 [**FMB (Functional Manipulation Benchmark)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.08553 "FMB: a Functional Manipulation Benchmark for Generalizable Robotic Learning") · 2024-01 · UC Berkeley — Real-world benchmark of functional manipulation with procedurally generated 3D-printed objects covering grasping, repositioning and assembly skills composed into multi-stage tasks; ships data, CAD files and imitation-learning baselines. _Note: IJRR 2024._ [code](https://github.com/rail-berkeley/fmb) · [project](https://functional-manipulation-benchmark.github.io)

**2023**

- 🟢 [**LIBERO**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.03310 "LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning") · 2023-06 · UT Austin et al. — Lifelong robot-learning benchmark with a procedural task generator and four suites (130 tasks: Spatial, Object, Goal, LIBERO-100) with teleoperated demos; widely adopted as the standard simulation benchmark for VLA fine-tuning. _Note: Near-saturated standard scores motivated LIBERO-PRO, LIBERO-Plus and LIBERO-X (listed separately)._ [code](https://github.com/Lifelong-Robot-Learning/LIBERO) · [project](https://libero-project.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**HomeRobot OVMM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11565 "HomeRobot: Open-Vocabulary Mobile Manipulation") · 2023-06 · Meta FAIR et al. — Open-vocabulary mobile manipulation benchmark (pick any object in an unseen home and place it on a named receptacle) with a simulation track in multi-room homes and a real-world software stack for the low-cost Hello Robot Stretch. [code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/home-robot) · [project](https://ovmm.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**FurnitureBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.12821 "FurnitureBench: Reproducible Real-World Benchmark for Long-Horizon Complex Manipulation") · 2023-05 — Reproducible real-world furniture-assembly benchmark for long-horizon manipulation: 3D-printable furniture, a setup guide, 200+ hours (5,000+) of demonstrations, systematic task initialization, and the FurnitureSim simulator. _Note: RSS 2023._ [code](https://github.com/clvrai/furniture-bench) · [project](https://clvrai.com/furniture-bench)
- 🟢 [**ManiSkill2**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04659 "ManiSkill2: A Unified Benchmark for Generalizable Manipulation Skills") · 2023-02 · UC San Diego — Unified manipulation-skill benchmark with 20 task families, 2,000+ object models and 4M+ demonstration frames across stationary/mobile, single/dual-arm and rigid/soft-body tasks under one interface and evaluation protocol. _Note: ICLR 2023. The repo now hosts ManiSkill3 (arXiv 2410.00425), the GPU-parallel simulator successor, which belongs under sim._ [code](https://github.com/haosulab/ManiSkill) · [project](https://maniskill.ai/)

**2022**

- 🟢 [**VLMbench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08522 "VLMbench: A Compositional Benchmark for Vision-and-Language Manipulation") · 2022-06 · UC Santa Cruz — Compositional vision-and-language manipulation benchmark generated by the AMSolver system: templated tasks with language constraints (e.g., keep a mug upright), varied objects and automatic demonstrations, plus a 6D-CLIPort baseline. [code](https://github.com/eric-ai-lab/VLMbench)

**2021**

- 🟢 [**CALVIN**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03227 "CALVIN: A Benchmark for Language-Conditioned Policy Learning for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation Tasks") · 2021-12 · University of Freiburg — Open-source simulated benchmark for long-horizon, language-conditioned manipulation from onboard sensors: agents chain free-form instructions and are tested zero-shot on novel instructions, environments and objects. _Note: Maintains a leaderboard on its project site; RA-L 2022._ [code](https://github.com/mees/calvin) · [project](https://calvin.cs.uni-freiburg.de)

**2020**

- 🟢 [**ALFWorld**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.03768 "ALFWorld: Aligning Text and Embodied Environments for Interactive Learning") · 2020-10 · Microsoft Research; University of Washington — Aligns TextWorld text games with the visually grounded ALFRED household tasks so agents can learn abstract text-level policies and then execute them in the embodied environment; a common text-based testbed for LLM agent loops. _Note: ICLR 2021._ [code](https://github.com/alfworld/alfworld) · [project](https://alfworld.github.io/)

**2019**

- 🟢 [**ALFRED**](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.01734 "ALFRED: A Benchmark for Interpreting Grounded Instructions for Everyday Tasks") · 2019-12 · University of Washington; AI2 — Household instruction-following benchmark in AI2-THOR: 25k natural-language directives (high-level goals plus step-by-step instructions) paired with expert demonstrations of long, compositional tasks with irreversible state changes. _Note: Maintains a public leaderboard on askforalfred.com; CVPR 2020._ [code](https://github.com/askforalfred/alfred) · [project](https://askforalfred.com/)
- 🟢 [**Meta-World**](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10897 "Meta-World: A Benchmark and Evaluation for Multi-Task and Meta Reinforcement Learning") · 2019-10 · Stanford University; UC Berkeley — 50 distinct simulated robotic manipulation tasks for multi-task and meta-reinforcement learning with standardized evaluation protocols; now maintained by the Farama Foundation. _Note: CoRL 2019._ [code](https://github.com/Farama-Foundation/Metaworld) · [project](https://meta-world.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**RLBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.12271 "RLBench: The Robot Learning Benchmark & Learning Environment") · 2019-09 · Imperial College London — 100 hand-designed simulated manipulation tasks (CoppeliaSim/PyRep), from reaching to multi-stage chores, with RGB-D and mask observations and unlimited motion-planned demonstrations; a standard testbed for multi-task manipulation policies. [code](https://github.com/stepjam/RLBench) · [project](https://sites.google.com/view/rlbench)
